title: I go camping alone every fall. This year, every morning there was one more pair of boots outside my tent.
transcript:
I go camping alone every fall. This year, every morning there was one more pair of boots outside my tent. The first morning, I unzipped the tent and found my boots where I'd left them, and right beside them, a second pair. Same brand, same size, caked in the same red mud from the trail.

I figured another hiker had mixed things up in the dark. But the nearest campsite was two miles back, and there was no other tent.

The second morning, there were three pairs. All mine. My laces, double knotted the way I always do them. The left heel worn down, the way mine is worn.

I packed up and hiked out fast. I didn't stop until dusk, and I pitched the tent in a different valley entirely.

That night I didn't sleep. Just before dawn, I heard footsteps circling the tent. Slow. Heavy. Then they stopped, and I heard someone sit down outside and start unlacing a pair of boots.

Then someone else. Then someone else.

Four pairs, set down neatly in a row.

I looked at my own boots, right beside my sleeping bag, clean and dry. Then I looked at my bare feet.

They were caked in red mud.

Outside, someone tapped on the tent wall, and whispered in my own voice.

"Your turn."
